questions.stem: According to the handbook, what is the fundamental definition of food?

options.A: Any solid substance used to satisfy hunger
options.B: Any substance, solid or liquid, which when ingested can satisfy hunger, supply energy, and maintain metabolic processes
options.C: Chemical components that are vital for growth and maintenance of a healthy body
options.D: A substance primarily used to provide energy for physical exercise

questions.explanation: The handbook defines food as any substance (solid or liquid) that performs three functions: satisfies hunger, supplies energy, and maintains metabolic processes.

questions.stem: How does the text define the science of nutrition?

options.A: The study of cooking techniques and pastry production
options.B: The study of essential nutrients and how they are cooked
options.C: The science of food, nutrients, and their action, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease
options.D: The process of categorizing kitchen equipment and hygiene

questions.explanation: Nutrition is specifically defined as the science of food, nutrients, and the substances therein, including their balance in relation to health and disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the WHO definition of health as provided in the document?

options.A: The mere absence of disease or infirmity
options.B: A state of physical fitness achieved through proper nutrition
options.C: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.D: The ability of the body to repair worn out tissues

questions.explanation: The World Health Organisation defines health as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not just the absence of disease.

questions.stem: What are the six basic classes of nutrients listed in the handbook?

options.A: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals, and water
options.B: Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, roughages, vitamins, and minerals
options.C: Energy-givers, growth-promoters, regulators, water, fiber, and lipids
options.D: Glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, and water

questions.explanation: The handbook explicitly lists these six as the basic classes of nutrients.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of roughages according to the text?

options.B: To assist bowel movement
options.C: To promote the growth of bone tissue

questions.explanation: While some classify roughages as nutrients, the text notes they primarily function to assist bowel movement.

questions.stem: Which nutrients are categorized specifically as 'Energy-giving nutrients'?

options.B: Carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids

questions.explanation: The functional category for energy provision includes carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids (fats and oil).

questions.stem: Which nutrient class does NOT participate in regulating body processes or promoting growth and development?

options.B: Vitamins

questions.explanation: According to the functional categories listed, carbohydrates are only listed under energy-giving, whereas proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, and water are listed for growth and regulation.

questions.stem: What two characteristics are required for a nutrient to be considered 'essential'?

options.A: It must provide energy and be found in all food groups
options.B: It must be ingested in large quantities and be easily digested
options.C: Its omission leads to health decline, and its restoration regains normal function
options.D: It must be a mineral and must be soluble in water

questions.explanation: A nutrient is essential if its absence causes health problems that can be reversed by adding the nutrient back before permanent damage occurs.

questions.stem: How is 'Kitchen Equipment' distinguished from 'Kitchen Utensils'?

options.A: Equipment is used for cooking; utensils are used for eating
options.B: Equipment refers to big, often fixed items; utensils are small, easily moved items
options.C: Equipment is always electric; utensils are always manual
options.D: Equipment is made of metal; utensils are made of plastic or wood

questions.explanation: Kitchen equipment includes big items like refrigerators or sinks that aren't easily moved, while utensils are light, portable items like pots and knives.

questions.stem: Which of the following is categorized as 'Mechanical equipment'?

options.B: Mincers and mixers

questions.explanation: The handbook categorizes potato peelers, mincers, mixers, refrigerators, and dishwashers as mechanical equipment.

questions.stem: Which hygiene practice is required for a person working in the kitchen regarding their physical appearance?

options.A: Wearing high-heeled shoes for better posture
options.B: Wearing dropping jewelleries for professional identification
options.D: Keeping hands uncovered even if they have cuts

questions.explanation: Kitchen hygiene rules state that long or painted nails should not be worn by anybody handling food.

questions.stem: A chef uses a microwave to cook food. Which principle of heat transfer is primarily being used?

options.B: Convection

questions.explanation: Radiation is the transfer of heat by electromagnetic waves, such as microwave and infrared waves.

questions.stem: Which cooking method relies on heat passing through a medium (liquid or gas) via currents?

options.B: Convection

questions.explanation: In convection, heat passes through a medium (liquid or gas) and is distributed by convection currents.

questions.stem: Which group of cooking methods all utilize the principle of 'Dry Heat'?

options.B: Roasting, baking, and grilling

questions.explanation: Roasting, baking, and grilling are methods of cooking by dry heat (radiant heat).

questions.stem: What is the defining characteristic of 'Poaching' as a moist heat method?

options.A: Cooking in a liquid at 212 degrees Fahrenheit
options.B: Cooking food in a liquid at just below boiling point (180-185°F)
options.C: Surrounding food in a vapor bath
options.D: Cooking food in a small amount of fat in a shallow pan

questions.explanation: Poaching involves submerging food in a liquid at a low temperature (180 to 185 degrees Fahrenheit) where the liquid is shivering without air bubbles breaking the surface.

questions.stem: How does 'Boiling' differ from 'Simmering'?

options.A: Boiling occurs at 185°F, while simmering occurs at 212°F
options.B: Boiling bubbles rapidly break the surface; simmering bubbles are just off the boil (185-200°F)
options.C: Boiling is a dry heat method; simmering is moist heat
options.D: Simmering is used for bread; boiling is used for cookies

questions.explanation: Boiling is at 212°F with rapidly breaking bubbles, while simmering is between 185-200°F with slightly less action.

questions.stem: Which method is a 'Combination Method' using both dry and moist heat?

options.B: Shallow Poaching

questions.explanation: Braising is a combination method where food is seared (dry heat) and then cooked covered with a small amount of liquid (moist heat).

questions.stem: What is the standard proportion of fat to flour in short pastry?
questions.explanation: The handbook notes that for any short pastry, the proportion of fat to flour is 1:2.

questions.stem: If a pastry turns out 'too hard', what is a likely reason according to the handbook?

options.B: There is too much water
options.D: Fat was rubbed in too much

questions.explanation: One of the possible reasons for hard pastry is having too much water (or too little fat/too much handling).

questions.stem: Which raising agent relies on minute fungi fermenting sugar to produce carbon dioxide?

options.B: Cream of tartar

questions.explanation: Yeast consists of minute fungi that ferment sugar to produce carbon dioxide and alcohol.

questions.stem: In yeast fermentation, which enzyme converts soluble starch into maltose and dextrin?

options.B: Maltose

questions.explanation: Diastase is the enzyme present in yeast and flour that converts soluble starch into maltose and dextrin.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of 'creaming fat and sugar' in cake making?

options.B: To incorporate air mechanically as a raising agent
options.D: To prevent the gluten from stretching

questions.explanation: Air is incorporated mechanically through processes like creaming of fat and sugar or whisking eggs.

questions.stem: When baking a large fruit cake, why should you avoid slamming the oven door?

options.A: It might cause the cherries to sink to the bottom
options.B: The inrush of cold air may cause the mixture to rise unevenly
options.D: It prevents the radiation from reaching the cake

questions.explanation: The text warns that an inrush of cold air from slamming the door checks the rising and causes unevenness.

questions.stem: According to the short pastry recipe, how much fat (total) is needed for 200g of flour?
questions.explanation: The recipe for 200g of flour calls for 50g of lard/vegetable fat and 50g of butter/margarine, totaling 100g. This follows the 1:2 fat-to-flour ratio.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a 'balanced diet'?

options.A: A meal containing carbohydrates and proteins only
options.B: A diet that provides all six classes of nutrients in correct proportions
options.C: A diet high in energy-giving foods for active individuals
options.D: A diet free from fats and oils

questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies all essential nutrients in the right amounts to maintain health and proper body function.

questions.stem: Which nutrient is primarily responsible for building and repairing worn-out body tissues?

options.B: Proteins

questions.explanation: Proteins are body-building nutrients responsible for growth, repair, and maintenance of tissues.

questions.stem: Which nutrient plays a major role in regulating body processes without supplying energy?

options.B: Carbohydrates

questions.explanation: Vitamins regulate metabolic processes but do not supply energy.

questions.stem: What is one key function of water in the body?

options.B: Acting as a medium for chemical reactions and transportation of nutrients

questions.explanation: Water serves as a solvent and transport medium for nutrients and waste products in the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as large kitchen equipment?

options.B: Knife

questions.explanation: Large kitchen equipment includes heavy, fixed items such as refrigerators, sinks, and cupboards.

questions.stem: Which safety practice helps prevent fire accidents in the kitchen?

options.B: Storing flammable materials near the stove
options.C: Keeping a fire blanket or extinguisher accessible

questions.explanation: Fire safety equipment must be accessible to control accidental kitchen fires.

questions.stem: Which example best illustrates heat transfer by conduction?

options.B: Hot air circulating in an oven
options.C: A metal spoon becoming hot in a pot of soup

questions.explanation: Conduction is heat transfer through direct contact between particles.

questions.stem: Steaming differs from boiling because steaming:

options.B: Cooks food by surrounding it with vapor rather than submerging it in water

questions.explanation: Steaming uses vapor (steam) to cook food instead of immersing it in liquid.

questions.stem: Which factor can cause pastry to become soggy?

options.B: Insufficient baking time
options.D: Low oven temperature at the start

questions.explanation: If the oven is not hot enough, the pastry may not set quickly, resulting in sogginess.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of kneading in yeast dough preparation?

options.B: To develop gluten and trap gas produced during fermentation

questions.explanation: Kneading develops gluten structure, allowing the dough to retain carbon dioxide produced by yeast.

questions.stem: Which condition would most likely slow down yeast fermentation?

options.B: Presence of sugar

questions.explanation: Yeast activity slows significantly in cold conditions.

questions.stem: Deep frying differs from shallow frying because deep frying:

options.B: Submerges food completely in hot fat or oil

questions.explanation: In deep frying, food is fully immersed in hot fat, unlike shallow frying.

questions.stem: Which hygiene rule reduces the risk of food contamination from hair?

options.B: Using strong perfume

questions.explanation: Hair must be covered to prevent contamination of food.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why carbohydrates are classified mainly as energy-giving nutrients?

options.B: They form antibodies
options.C: They are broken down into glucose to supply fuel for the body

questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are converted into glucose, the body's primary energy source.

questions.stem: Why is it important not to over-handle short pastry?

options.B: It activates yeast
options.C: It develops too much gluten, making the pastry tough

questions.explanation: Excess handling develops gluten, resulting in a hard or tough pastry.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of minerals in the body?

options.A: They provide the highest concentration of energy per gram
options.B: They regulate body processes and contribute to structural components like bones and teeth
options.C: They serve only as digestive lubricants
options.D: They are converted directly into glucose

questions.explanation: Minerals help regulate physiological functions and form structural parts such as bones and teeth.

questions.stem: Although lipids are classified as energy-giving nutrients, they are also important because they:

options.B: Provide insulation and protect vital organs

questions.explanation: Beyond energy supply, lipids insulate the body and cushion vital organs.

questions.stem: Which practice most directly prevents cross-contamination in the kitchen?

options.A: Using the same knife for raw meat and vegetables
options.B: Storing cooked food beside raw meat
options.C: Washing hands after handling raw food before touching cooked food

questions.explanation: Proper handwashing between handling raw and cooked food prevents transfer of harmful microorganisms.

questions.stem: Which cooking method would be most suitable for tough cuts of meat that require slow tenderization?

options.B: Deep frying

questions.explanation: Braising uses moist heat over time, breaking down connective tissues in tougher meats.

questions.stem: Which raising agent produces carbon dioxide through a chemical reaction when moistened and heated?

options.B: Baking powder

questions.explanation: Baking powder releases carbon dioxide through chemical reactions when combined with liquid and heat.

questions.stem: If yeast dough fails to rise properly, which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.A: Excessively hot water that kills the yeast
options.B: Insufficient kneading

questions.explanation: High temperatures can destroy yeast cells, preventing fermentation and gas production.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key difference between dry heat and moist heat cooking methods?

options.A: Dry heat uses liquid as a cooking medium
options.B: Moist heat methods involve water or steam as the heat transfer medium
options.C: Dry heat always cooks faster than moist heat

questions.explanation: Moist heat cooking relies on water or steam to transfer heat to the food.

questions.stem: Why is temperature control important during deep frying?

options.B: If the oil is too cool, food absorbs excess fat
options.D: Oil temperature does not affect quality

questions.explanation: When oil temperature is too low, food absorbs more fat, resulting in greasy products.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why hygiene is critical in food preparation?

options.A: It improves the color of food
options.B: It prevents foodborne illnesses caused by microorganisms
options.C: It increases the nutritional value of food

questions.explanation: Poor hygiene can lead to contamination and foodborne diseases.

questions.stem: Which of the following links nutrition directly to overall health?

options.A: Proper nutrient balance supports physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: Eating large quantities of food improves strength
options.D: Only energy-giving foods determine health status

questions.explanation: Nutrition influences total well-being, aligning with the definition of health as complete physical, mental, and social wellness.
